FIELD NOTE 001 · HUSHPOD · OCTOBER 2026

The sound that
was still there.

Quiet does not always mean still. Two oscillators can keep moving while the signal we listen to disappears.

THE OBSERVATION
We hear a combination,
not the whole system.
Imagine two equal signals arriving with opposite signs. Their sum is zero. Neither signal has to be zero on its own. In Hushpod, that distinction is something you can play.
Each of the three pockets has a complex amplitude: a size and a phase. The two waists set the strength of exchange between neighbors. Our pickup listens to one weighted combination of all three. It can miss motion that cancels in that combination.
Silence at one pickup is a statement about that pickup.
It is not a measurement of everything inside.
The quiet preset is deliberately symmetric: equal outer amplitudes, opposite phases, an empty middle, and equally open waists. The contributions driving the middle cancel too. Both ends continue rotating and decaying together. Narrowing one waist breaks that balance; the model can redistribute existing action and produce a nonzero pickup without adding an impulse.


WHAT THE MODEL SAYS
Action is not energy in joules.
We call N = |a₁|² + |a₂|² + |a₃|² oscillator action. It measures squared amplitude in this model’s units. We have not calibrated it to mechanical energy, displacement, sound pressure, or perceived loudness.
Coupling moves action between pockets according to their relative phases. With no input or damping, it conserves total action. Here, natural amplitude damping is 0.045 per second, so total action falls as N(t) = 0.5 e−0.09t, even when the pickup is silent.
The model is nonlinear: each pocket’s phase rate also depends on its own action. At unequal, sufficiently high amplitudes, this detuning can inhibit exchange—often called nonlinear trapping. That is distinct from the phase cancellation demonstrated here; this entry does not establish a trapping threshold.


Equations, parameters & numerical method
With no rub or hold, the rotating-frame equation is:
daⱼ/dt = −γaⱼ − iβ|aⱼ|²aⱼ − i ∑ₖ Kⱼₖaₖ
Only neighboring pockets are coupled. K₁₂ = K₂₁ = 4u₁ and K₂₃ = K₃₂ = 4u₂; β = 16, γ = 0.045, and waist openness u is between 0 and 1. Waist targets relax with a 22 ms time constant.
The preset is a = (0.5, 0, −0.5), with both u = 1. The phase control replaces the last amplitude by 0.5 exp(iθ). “Narrow” sets the left target to 0.2; the right remains 1. No rub, hold, or impulses are applied during a run. Each run stops at 12 simulation seconds.
The pickup is p = a₁ + 0.35a₂ + a₃. The normalized pickup fraction is C = |p|² / (2.1225N), bounded between 0 and 1 by Cauchy–Schwarz. It is neither a fraction of mechanical energy emitted nor a loudness percentage.
The authoritative Pod implementation uses exact coupling evolution between local half steps, at 4,000 steps per simulation second. Sound interpolates the pickup onto a 220 Hz carrier, then applies the instrument’s fixed 0.78 tanh(1.4 × signal) saturation and this page’s fixed 0.35 volume. There is no added voice, recording, or automatic gain compensation.
Silent mode runs the same model on the main thread. Listening transfers the current state to an AudioWorklet; its own measurements drive the display. Pause, hidden tabs and navigation stop sound. A delayed visual frame may slow silent simulation rather than catching up to wall time.


EVIDENCE / LIMITS
A claim you can check.
At the prepared starting instant, both aligned and opposite states have N = 0.5. The aligned state has |p|² = 1; the opposite state has |p|² ≈ 0. After eight seconds, the symmetric quiet state retains about 48.7% of its starting action while the pickup remains numerically negligible.
Those are numerical results for a specified initial state, not observations of a physical object. Exact cancellation relies on symmetry. Small phase errors, unequal damping or a different pickup can reveal motion; try 170° instead of 180°. A quiet speaker can also result from muted audio, which is why the pickup meter is measured before volume.
This is coherent coupled-mode synthesis, not a fluid, membrane or mass-spring solver. Its drawn pockets are explanatory graphics. The journal does not claim physical validation, scientific novelty, or peer review.
Reproducible model checks cover decay, cancellation, phase comparison, waist release and timestep convergence. The verification record separates automated browser checks from device-testing gaps. Real iPhone/iPad Safari audio interruptions, Android hardware sleep, speaker audibility and assistive-technology use still need hands-on testing.
